toegepas.voor: Die roer maak van die twee een dik pap sonder klonte.
toegepas.na: Deur te roer word die twee een dik pap sonder klonte.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The nominalised 'Die roer' as subject is stiff and can be misread; a verbal construction reads more naturally.
toegepas.fout: The nominalised subject 'Die roer' is stiff, and a Grade 5 reader may first read 'roer' as the noun (rudder, gun).
toegepas.rede_keurder: The verbal construction reads naturally and keeps the same claim that stirring turns the two into one lump-free paste.

toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Both clauses have their own subject and verb ('Die pap bly', 'dit word'), so AWS 2017 requires the comma.

toegepas.voor: Die pap gaan tussen planke en dit verhard
toegepas.na: Die pap gaan tussen planke in, en dit verhard
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'gaan tussen planke' needs 'in' to complete the movement, and AWS requires a comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
toegepas.fout: 'gaan tussen planke' leaves the movement unfinished, and the AWS comma before the clause-joining 'en' is missing.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'tussen planke in' completes the movement without changing where the paste goes, and both clauses have their own subject and verb, so the comma belongs.

toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma marks the second clause ('dit loop') and separates it from 'droog en los', where no comma belongs.

toegepas.rede_keurder: Two main clauses, the second with its own subject and verb; the comma also stops 'by' being read with what follows.

laat_vaar.voor: wat jy kan uitgooi soos meel
laat_vaar.na: wat jy soos meel kan uitgooi
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The comparison sits more naturally before the verb cluster in an Afrikaans subordinate clause.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: A 'soos' comparison placed after the verb cluster is normal Afrikaans; the reorder is lateral.

laat_vaar.voor: strooi die poeier stadig daarby in
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'daarby in' is an awkward combination; 'daarin' says plainly that the powder goes into the water.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'daarby in' is ordinary recipe Afrikaans and carries the sense of adding to the water; 'daarin' drops that and is no clearer.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two coordinate adjectives that each describe the noun are separated by a comma.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Afrikaans commonly writes stacked adjectives without a comma, and the lesson already writes 'droë wit poeier' without one; the comma is lateral and inconsistent.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In written standard Afrikaans an object such as a brick is referred to with 'dit', not the colloquial 'hy'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'hy' for a concrete object such as a brick is standard Afrikaans, the lesson uses 'sy' for the jelly elsewhere, and 'dit' in the sentence before already refers to the clay.

laat_vaar.blok: Wat verander en wat bly dieselfde
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The accent on 'ná' marks the time meaning 'after', set against 'voor', as AWS allows for clarity.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Set against 'voor', the temporal 'na' is already clear, so AWS does not call for the accent, and the lesson writes 'na' without one elsewhere.

na_skrywer.voor: Die meng alleen maak dus reeds 'n gom.
na_skrywer.na: Net deur te meng kry jy dus reeds 'n gom.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The nominal subject 'Die meng alleen' is wooden; a verbal phrase keeps the same meaning (mixing only, nothing more) and reads naturally.
na_skrywer.fout: The nominalised subject 'Die meng alleen' is wooden.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: 'Net deur te meng' can be read as 'only by mixing' (mixing is the only way to get glue) rather than 'mixing alone is enough', so the fix needs other wording.

na_skrywer.voor: Jellie is na die tyd nog nat

na_skrywer.rede_keurder: Straight after the sentence about comparing properties, 'daarna' could read as 'after comparing' instead of 'after the mixing', so the fault needs wording that keeps the time reference clear.

vlae.rede: Read on its own, the entry never names a powder before 'die poeier'; the first sentence only implies it through 'fyn te maal'. Making the link explicit would mean adding wording to the definition, so this is left for the reviewer or writer.
